SB19 returns to North America for the "Simula at Wakas" (SAW) World Tour starting with its San Francisco stop in less than five days. While I would have loved it had they chosen either a bigger venue or a Day 2 for any of SAW's three California stops, several things stop me from feeling shortchanged:

1. They have a tight schedule. Looking at the 5-day gap between Los Angeles and Toronto, we need to consider two things: travel and rehearsals. So that leaves us with three days. Historically, when in LA, SB19 allocates a day or two for Wish USA, a TV guesting, and a possible fan meet/surprise busking.

2. While they can possibly insert a Day 2 for LA after the activities mentioned on #1, would it make sense to follow up with a Day 2 on a Monday, July 14, even the following day? The day of the week, the rush hour traffic for which LA and its surrounding cities are notorious... it can be a huge risk.

3. Concert venues, according to a https://t.co/9xqKrI56Co article, are typically booked at least three (smaller venue) to six months (larger venue) in advance to accommodate both the location reservation and ticketing. Summer is peak concert season in the US. While there's no reservation for The Grove of Anaheim from July 14 to July 16 and while 1Z and Star Media could have most likely assessed the possibility of adding a Day 2 given that LA tickets sold out in five minutes, we'll just go back to #1 and the risk presented by #2.

These lead me to wondering if there will ever be a US East Coast stop. It's practically a crime, if I'm being dramatic (which I am) to not add at least one East Coast concert for SAW. Rumors have it that producers are fighting for the chance to bring it to New York for a possible second leg of the SAW World Tour  -   which would make sense given it was in New York that they recorded "Moonlight", shot the VEVO videos for "Gento" and "I Want You", and Sony Music's HQ is, well, in the city. Right now, I don't know what else to think regarding that.

We have our grievances. Nothing is invalid as all of us can see just how in demand SB19 have become. I, myself, feel like it's insane they're on their third year at Fox Theatre in Redwood City when there's a good chance they can fill to capacity Chase Center's 18,000 seats (where Jo Koy has had multiple sold out shows) or the smaller Bill Graham Civic Auditorium with its 5,000 to 8,000 seats.

After all that, I'm still confronted with the fact that them choosing to play it safe with smaller venues to consider ticket cost and investments is valid, too. They've just recovered from their most massive financial setback to date. I'm fairly certain that's one of the things they've considered in planning these things.

For now, let's pray for a safe flight and stay in the US for them and their team. If you're aware of what's been happening, here, you'd know what I mean. We can go back to our concerns once they're safely back in the Philippines in August.

@SB19Official #SB19
